indicators.note: in tells us one word goes inside the other, here the word for change within the word for friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend
to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: Someone pondering whether to alter something about a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply, which is what contemplating means.

clue.text: City set up in my recollection

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed city goes between the letters of my
set up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a city they once built.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory is something recalled, a recollection.

clue.text: Milk-maker first dated by casual girl

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of dated is used

parts.note: airy means casual or offhand
a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A carefree girl going out with a dairy worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman who works in a dairy making butter and cheese from milk, so she produces milk products.

definitions.meaning: the word 'some' spoken aloud is 'sum', meaning an amount added up

explanation.surface: A remark about part of something being claimed as the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works by sound: 'Some said' is 'sum', which is a synonym of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an amount added up; and whole means complete or entire, both senses of this word.

definitions.meaning: a dessert of sponge, custard and cream, a British pudding
matters of no importance, little things

explanation.surface: Endearments whispered between lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet nothings' reads as lovers' talk; split it, and a trifle is a British layered dessert and also something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a sponge-and-custard pudding and also something of little worth.

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of artist are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter has switched television stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage, a natural channel between two bodies of water.

clue.text: Decay reversed by teacher and bully

indicators.note: reversed tells us the word for decay is read backwards

parts.note: rot is decay
a mentor is a guide or teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher stopping decay and also a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who persecutes others, much like a bully.

indicators.note: centred means the letter for soft is put in the middle of the rearranged meal
cooked tells us the letters of meal are mixed up, as ingredients are

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A hearty meal with a soft filling, generously served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' turns MEAL into AMLE, and 'centred' puts P in its middle: AM-P-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, which is plentiful.

clue.text: Records attempt to produce decorative fabric

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying out recordings in order to make a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile with a pictorial design, hung as decoration.

clue.text: Keep most important volunteers at home

parts.note: the main thing is the most important one
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Advice to retain the key volunteers by keeping them at home.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going or keep it in good condition.

indicators.note: contrary means the word for beast faces the other way, read backwards

parts.note: an orc is a monstrous beast of fantasy
a pup is a young animal, a youngster

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal and its young turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' looks like a description of the beast's temper, but it is the reversal signal; the beast is a fantasy monster.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop up is to arise or turn up unexpectedly, a synonym for appear.

indicators.note: around means the word for bug goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: to tap a phone is to bug it

indicators.note: mid- means the centre letter of afternoon is taken

explanation.surface: An insect lying in wait in the middle of the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests an insect but is the eavesdropping verb, TAP; R is the middle of the nine letters of afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them unawares, as an ambush does.

indicators.note: around means the pair of words for place and gold, run together, are turned back to front

parts.note: to lay something is to place it
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An instruction to set gold round a monarch, perhaps as a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the whole of LAYOR backwards; OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal is used as an adjective meaning sovereign, belonging to a monarch.

clue.text: Size of girl with broken green heart

indicators.note: heart means the rearranged letters form the middle of the word for girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: broken tells us the letters of green are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A lovelorn girl's broken heart, described in terms of size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' looks like part of a romantic surface, but it tells us where the jumbled letters go: inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness is the quality of being big, which is a measure of size.

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it stands for many
anti means opposed to
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A crowd taking a stand against a tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis, or praying mantis, is a predatory insect.

clue.text: Essays about one record or sets of three

indicators.note: about tells us the word for essays goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: to essay is to try, so essays are tries
I is the Roman numeral one
a log is a record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Essays on a single record, or perhaps three-part works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' looks like the noun, but it is the verb: to essay is to attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a group of three related works, so trilogies are sets of three.

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for irritation sits within the word for 'for each'

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: Each athlete feels an annoying itch somewhere inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball and cricket a pitcher is the player who delivers the ball, a sportsman.

parts.note: hid is the past tense of hide, meaning concealed
the head of egg is its first letter
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: An intellectual hiding in a secret spring, too closed-minded to emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' suggests an intellectual, but it is just the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidebound person is set in their ways, unable to accept new ideas.

clue.text: Poem edited by one in strange shop

indicators.note: edited means the letters of poem are rearranged, as when a text is reworked
in tells us the numeral one goes inside the word for strange

parts.note: rum is old British slang for strange or odd
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A poem revised by someone in an odd little shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' turns POEM into EMPO; RUM is dated British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop or trading centre.

parts.note: made means manufactured
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was a paramilitary group

explanation.surface: A claim that an island was created by terrorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is an Atlantic island belonging to Portugal.

clue.text: An affirmative, or more than one

definitions.text: An affirmative, or more than one

parts.words: An affirmative, or more than one
parts.note: read as one yes vote, then as the plural for several such votes in a division

explanation.surface: A vote being counted: one yes, or several.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons a yes vote has its own old word, and the votes in favour are counted under its plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayes are votes in favour, the plural of the parliamentary yes.

indicators.note: beyond says the word for cycle comes after the abbreviation for thoroughfare

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare
to ride is to cycle

explanation.surface: Choosing whether to walk or bike past the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, so to stride is to walk purposefully.

clue.text: Sounds upset about third position: sitting

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the chosen letter
upset in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: noises are sounds

indicators.note: third tells us to take only the third letter of position

explanation.surface: Upset noises about where someone is placed in a seated arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOISES into SESION; the third letter of 'position' is S, which goes inside to make SES-S-ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period of meeting, as a sitting of a court or parliament.

indicators.note: clad means the colour word dresses round the worker

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a worker is a worker ant

explanation.surface: An employee in red uniform grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to speak angrily at length, a loud form of complaint.

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
a dish is an attractive person, as is a looker

explanation.surface: Television viewers busy at the sink with the washing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishes' suggests plates, but in slang a dish is a good-looking person, a looker.
explanation.definitionFit: Onlookers are spectators, people watching something happen.

clue.text: Stick-up with a letter opener is permitted

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for stick reads upwards

parts.note: gel means to stick together, to set

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word letter is used

explanation.surface: A robbery using a paper knife, oddly declared lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick-up' suggests a robbery, but 'up' reverses GEL to LEG; 'letter opener' is the first letter of letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means allowed by law, that is permitted.

clue.text: Left one beside a North African country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
by means beside, as in 'by the sea'

explanation.surface: Someone left alone next to a country in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a country on the north coast of Africa, between Egypt and Tunisia.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid ignited by soldier

parts.note: lit means set alight, ignited
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier setting fire to some fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume, used to measure liquids.

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, as of the actress Bergman
where a solver writes the answer: inside the crossword's grid

explanation.surface: A woman being told where to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the name into two words: the girl is placed in the grid you are filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female given name; and split as two words it says where the entry goes.

clue.text: Have suspicions about fog and decay

parts.note: mist is a light fog
rust is the corrosion, or decay, of iron

explanation.surface: Distrust of weather and corrosion, as of an old car left outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to doubt or be wary of, which is having suspicions.

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can stand for model

explanation.surface: A badger watching a fashion model from hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harass or pester them, an old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Mean journalist to be one's fianc

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter planning to become engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one plans to marry, a betrothed.
